front: Your request flow is DNS -> AWS Load Balancer -> Nginx -> EC2 -> Docker -> application. You receive a 502 response. How will you debug it step by step?
back: A 502 means some hop returned an invalid gateway response — usually connection refused, reset, or crash mid-write — not a patient timeout. I correlate one request id across ALB and nginx, prove target health and local curl to the container, then fix the dead upstream before touching application business logic.

back: Intermittent 504s with green health are almost always a timeout-budget mismatch on the real path — slow dependency or saturated workers — not a dead process. I line up ALB and nginx timings for one request id, find which timer fired first, then fix the slow work instead of blindly raising every timeout.
